annotations.title: Developer utilities: cron, regex, UUID, slug and JSON

description: Developer utilities: cron, regex, UUID, slug and JSON. Use when a task needs one of the small developer answers that would otherwise cost a round trip to a web tool: the next times a cron expression fires (in a named time zone and in UTC, with a plain-English reading and a note on which non-standard extensions it uses), what a regular expression matches in a piece of text (run on RE2, so no pattern can backtrack its way into exponential time, and a pattern whose compiled program is too large for the input it was given is refused rather than run), fresh UUIDs (version 4, or time-ordered version 7), a URL slug for a title, or JSON pretty-printed, minified or key-sorted with the line and column of a syntax error. Free, and no data is kept. Free to call.

count.description: How many cron runs, or how many UUIDs, to return.

flags.description: Distinct letters from i, m, s and u, for regex_test.

indent.description: Spaces per level for json_format; 0 minifies.

input.description: The text to run the pattern over, for regex_test.

limit.description: Maximum matches to return, for regex_test.

max_length.description: Cap on the slug length, for slugify.

operation.description: One of cron_next_runs, regex_test, uuid, slugify, json_format. Each one reads its own further fields.

pattern.description: The regular expression, for regex_test. Run on RE2.

separator.description: The slug separator. Defaults to a hyphen.

start.description: ISO instant to start the cron walk from, for cron_next_runs.

text.description: The title to slugify, or the JSON document to format.

timezone.description: IANA time zone name for cron_next_runs, such as Europe/London. Defaults to UTC.

name: dev_utils
